subject.title: fix(reef): keep routine agent replies from disappearing

question: Should Reef treat code, logs, hostnames, non-secret configuration, and internal identifiers as allowable by default when no concrete secret is present?
rationale: This changes the intended DLP boundary rather than merely correcting implementation mechanics, so tests cannot establish which confidential-but-non-secret material maintainers intend Reef to transmit automatically.

options.title: Approve the narrowed boundary
options.body: Fix retry lifecycle ownership, expand the guard corpus for confidential-but-non-secret examples, and approve the new allow/review/deny policy before merge.

options.title: Retain fail-closed internal handling
options.body: Keep internal or confidential material in review or deny and narrow this PR to rejection visibility and durable recovery.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrowed boundary
recommendation.body: Fix retry lifecycle ownership, expand the guard corpus for confidential-but-non-secret examples, and approve the new allow/review/deny policy before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR is maintainer-labeled, self-assigned, and changes Reef's security policy as well as its delivery behavior.
